title.narrative: Socioeconomic resilience is built among the rural vulnerable including migrant families in the areas/ regions hardest hit by the COVID pandemic

description.narrative: The action is focused on enforcing the rights and entitlements of the vulnerable communities including women & children, primitive tribal communities, migrant workers, small & marginal farmers, and NTFP gatherers. Efforts are aligned with SDG Framework (SDG1) through the implementation of nationally appropriate social protection systems and measures. There shall be positive discrimination in favor of women and vulnerable sections while promoting equity, rights by collecting gendersegregated information to resource distribution. The actions ensure rights to economic resources, as well as access to basic services. With regard to issues of the migrants, it correlates with the human rights framework to offer them a life with dignity and selfesteem through skilling and enterprise promotion. Strong cooperation with the labor department will be achieved to deliver the social security and protection that the migrants are rightfully entitled to following good governance principles.

title.narrative: Increased Social security coverage at the HH level through enhanced access to welfare schemes and entitlements, targeting a minimum of 25% womenheaded households (WHH).

description.narrative: Increased HH income contributed through public programmes and ensured labour rights by migrant workers, targeting a minimum of 25% women migrant workers. CSO, Govt. and private sector platform (MAP) strengthened to contribute to the formation and implementation of enabling policies and rules in favour of migrant workers, ensuring the inclusion of women migrant workers in the formulation and implementation of policies and rules.

comment.narrative: This data is based on the project MIS and has been reported in the Annual narrative report for the year 2023 2nd year of operation
